title: Vendor Data Minimization & Usage Logging Annex (Template)
content:
Introduction:
This annex is intended to be attached to the Master Services Agreement or Data Processing Addendum between [Customer] and [Vendor] (the "Agreement"). It defines data minimization, usage logging, and audit evidence obligations that apply to vendor services that process customer content, API requests, or outputs produced by machine learning models (including inference, embeddings, and retraining inputs). The parties may adapt the annex to reflect product architecture and applicable law.

1. Definitions:
- "Customer Data": any data, text, prompt, response, embedding, metadata, or other content provided by Customer or generated by Customer's use of the Service.
- "Operational Logs": logs necessary for monitoring, debugging, billing, and capacity planning that may include request timestamps, model identifier, approximate token counts, latency, error codes, and anonymized routing decisions.
- "Usage Logs": a subset of Operational Logs that may include hashed or pseudonymized prompt identifiers, session identifiers, and non-content-derived feature vectors used for quality monitoring.
- "Sensitive Customer Data": Personal Data, regulated health or financial data, or any data identified by Customer as subject to heightened protection.

2. Purpose Limitation and Data Minimization:
- Vendor shall only collect Usage Logs and Operational Logs to the minimum extent necessary to provide, maintain, secure, and improve the Service, and to comply with the Agreement.
- Vendor shall not persist Customer Data content in logs unless explicitly agreed in writing and with Customer's prior consent for a narrowly scoped purpose (e.g., debugging a specific incident).
- For any collection of Customer Data content for debugging, Vendor shall implement one-time access tokens, time-limited retention (no longer than 30 days unless otherwise agreed), and documented approval from a named customer contact.

3. Permitted Fields in Usage and Operational Logs:
- Allowed non-content fields: request_id, timestamp (UTC), model_version, region, CPU/GPU node id (pseudonymized), latency_ms, token_count_estimate, status_code, error_message (non-sensitive), batching_group_id, cache_hit_boolean.
- Permitted pseudonymized identifiers: session_id (hashed with rotation), user_agent (trimmed), client_ip (truncated to remove last octet for IPv4; IPv6 analogous truncation).
- Prohibited content fields: raw prompt text, raw model output, attachments, or embedded files unless covered by explicit Customer consent.

4. Aggregation, Pseudonymization and Anonymization:
- Where logs are retained for analytics or product improvement, Vendor shall aggregate or pseudonymize values so that they cannot be reconstituted to identify the original Customer Data in normal operations.
- Vendor shall maintain key-management and documented procedures for any reversible pseudonymization; only personnel with Business Need and approval (change control) shall be able to perform re-identification for debugging.

5. Retention and Deletion:
- Default retention for Operational Logs: 90 days.
- Default retention for Usage Logs used for product analytics: 180 days, subject to aggregation after 30 days.
- Customer may request accelerated deletion of logs referencing Customer Data content; Vendor shall comply within 30 calendar days of validated request, unless subject to litigation hold or legal retention obligations, in which case Vendor will notify Customer.
- Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Vendor shall delete all Customer Data content from logs and backups within 60 days, except as otherwise required by law. The deletion schedule and certification process are described in Section 9.

6. Access Controls and Personnel Limitations:
- Access to raw logs that may contain Customer-identifying metadata is limited to authorized personnel on a least-privilege basis and requires approval from Security and the Customer Success contact for the affected Customer.
- Vendor personnel with access must undergo background screening and data protection training. Access records and justifications must be logged and available for audit (see Section 8).

7. Use of Logs for Model Improvement and Product Development:
- Vendor will not use Customer Data content from logs to train or improve models without explicit Customer opt-in via a written addendum.
- Aggregate telemetry (e.g., failure rates, latency percentiles) may be used without opt-in, provided Customer-identifying attributes are removed.

8. Audit Rights and Evidence:
- Customer has the right to request (quarterly or for-cause) evidence that Vendor's logging practices conform to this Annex. Such evidence can include:
  - Redacted log samples (with content removed) demonstrating field schemas and pseudonymization methods.
  - Access-control logs showing personnel access events and approvals.
  - Retention schedules and automated deletion logs (timestamps and counts).
  - Summaries of cryptographic key rotation and key-holder roles.
- Vendor will respond to routine evidence requests within 10 business days and for-cause requests within 5 business days. Requests that require significant engineering work may be subject to a reasonable cooperation fee, which will be agreed in advance.

9. Deletion Certification:
- Upon deletion requests or contract termination, Vendor will provide a Deletion Certificate within 30 days that includes: deletion time window, data categories deleted, verification steps performed, and a signed statement of compliance by the Security Officer.

10. Incident Handling and Notification:
- If a security incident impacts logs containing Customer Data or pseudonymization keys, Vendor will notify Customer within 72 hours of detection with a preliminary notification and provide a full technical report within 14 days.
- Notification will include: scope of data involved (log categories), root cause, mitigation steps taken, and steps to prevent recurrence.

11. Subprocessors and Transfers:
- Vendor will ensure contractual flow-down obligations to subprocessors with respect to data minimization, pseudonymization, retention, and audit support. Subprocessor lists will be provided on request and updated at least annually.
- Cross-border transfer of logs containing Customer Data content is prohibited unless Customer consents or functional necessity documented and appropriate safeguards (e.g., SCCs) are in place.

12. Exceptions and Business Continuity:
- For incident response or regulatory requirements, Vendor may temporarily retain additional log details beyond the standard retention periods, but must notify Customer, document the business need, and limit access and retention to the minimum necessary.

13. Dispute Resolution and Remedies:
- Material breaches of this Annex will be treated as material breaches of the Agreement. Customer's remedies include injunctive relief, contractual damages as specified in the Agreement, and audit/enforcement rights.

Appendix A — Log Field Schema (Example):
- request_id: string (UUID)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- model_version: string
- latency_ms: integer
- token_count_estimate: integer
- error_code: string (nullable)
- session_id_hash: string (truncated SHA256 with rotating salt id)
- client_region: string
- cache_hit: boolean

Appendix B — Short Form Checklist for Commercial Negotiations:
- Confirm default retention windows or customize per Customer requirement.
- Confirm whether Customer content may be included in any logging for debugging; require written consent.
- Ensure re-identification approval flow documented and Customer contact included.
- Verify subprocessors and cross-border transfer clauses align with policy.
- Add deletion certification timeline to SOW where necessary.

Notes/Work-in-progress:
- Placeholder: define maximum allowed plaintext snippets in logs (if any) — current recommendation: zero unless explicitly allowed.
- Placeholder: standard templates for Deletion Certificate and Evidence Package to be attached as exhibits.
